home.title: anistream · an open-source anime client
home.description: An open-source anime client for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Android TV, Windows, Linux and the terminal. It hosts no content.
home.scene.alt: A rooftop at dusk over a lit city, meteors crossing the sky, and Nagare, anistream’s mascot, looking up at them, drawn in terminal halfblocks
home.hero.title: Browse, watch, track and sync anime
home.hero.sub: Native apps for {{platforms}}, and one for the terminal. You add sources as plugins.
home.hero.note: MIT licence · Browsing needs no account
home.hero.caption: The Mac app going from Continue to a title page, with the iPhone app on a title page in front. Every title and picture here is made up.
home.hero.macVideoAlt: The Mac app on Continue: another show picked from the queue, its banner growing into the title page, then its second season
home.hero.macAlt: The Mac app’s Continue screen, with a banner for the show in progress and a button to resume its episode
home.hero.phoneAlt: The iPhone app on a title page, with the show’s banner, a button to resume episode 7 and the episode list
home.glance.label: Continue, the calendar and Play on TV
home.glance.continue.videoAlt: The Android app opening a show from Continue, switching to Season 2 and back, scrolling its episodes, then swiping back to Continue
home.glance.continue.title: Continue watching
home.glance.continue.text: The shows you’re partway through, with the next episode ready to play.
home.glance.calendar.videoAlt: The iPhone app’s calendar: the days of the week, then every show airing
home.glance.calendar.alt: The iPhone app on a title page
home.glance.calendar.title: Calendar and sync
home.glance.calendar.text: See what airs each day. Your progress syncs to AniList, MyAnimeList, Kitsu, Simkl and Trakt.
home.glance.tv.videoAlt: The iPhone app sending an episode to a TV, then pausing it as the remote
home.glance.tv.alt: The iPhone app as the TV’s remote
home.glance.tv.title: Play on TV
home.glance.tv.text: Send an episode to the Android TV app, then use your phone or computer as the remote.
home.apps.title: Apps
home.apps.lede: Each app is built with its platform’s toolkit: SwiftUI on Apple, Jetpack Compose on Android, WinUI 3 on Windows, GTK 4 on Linux and Ratatui in the terminal. They share one engine, written in Rust.
home.apps.linuxAlt: The Linux app on Continue, with the shows in progress beside the one picked and a button to resume its episode
home.apps.tvAlt: The Android TV app on Continue, with a large button to resume episode 7 and a row of shows in progress
home.apps.androidAlt: The Android app on Continue, with the show in progress and the shows that came out this week
home.player.title: The player
home.player.lede: Episodes play in mpv, with a skip button for the opening and Up Next at the end. Drag the line to compare a 480p stream, upscaled and not, with the 1080p original.
home.player.compareNote: Natural keeps the line work as it was drawn and comes closest to the original. Sharp draws the lines crisper and bolder than they were.
home.player.skipAlt: The show's logo during its opening, with a Skip opening button in the corner
home.player.skipCaption: A button to skip the opening.
home.player.menuAlt: The anistream menu inside the player: episodes, sources, sub or dub, upscaling, night mode, subtitles, audio
home.player.menuCaption: The player menu: episodes, sources, sub or dub, upscaling and tracks.
home.player.nextAlt: An Up Next card over the ending credits, naming episode 3.2 with a still from its preview
home.player.nextCaption: Up Next over the ending credits.
home.player.credit: These three are the terminal app’s player. Player frames from こうしす！ #3.1 and the comparison from #3.2, by OPAP-JP contributors, licensed CC BY 4.0.
home.terminal.title: The terminal app
home.terminal.lede: anistream also runs in a terminal on macOS, Linux and Windows. On a Mac it shares its history and config with the Mac app.
home.terminal.caption: The home screen, search, an episode list and playback. Covers show as images in Ghostty, Kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm and other terminals with image support.
home.terminal.alt: anistream running in a terminal: the home screen, a search, an episode list and an episode playing
home.terminal.vim.name: Vim keys
home.terminal.vim.text: hjkl or the arrow keys, and you can rebind them.
home.terminal.parties.name: Watch parties
home.terminal.parties.text: Press y to watch an episode with friends. Everyone’s player stays in sync.
home.terminal.cli.name: Command line
home.terminal.cli.text: --search, --stats and --random print JSON with --json, and --continue resumes the episode you left half watched.
home.sources.title: Sources
home.sources.anilist.name: AniList
home.sources.anilist.text: Public data for browsing, search, the calendar and title pages, with a pointer to where each title is licensed.
home.sources.plugins.name: Plugins
home.sources.plugins.text: For APIs you have the right to use, servers you host and media you own. anistream never circumvents DRM, so a licensed stream opens in the service that carries it.
home.sources.stores.name: Plugin stores
home.sources.stores.text: Run by someone you know, for the people they invite. anistream lists none of them.
home.sources.lede: Torrents are off by default and stay unreachable until you set up the VPN guard. What you point any source at is your decision and your risk, under the laws that apply to you. Removing a source takes one config edit.
home.install.title: Installation
home.install.lede: Every release has the apps and the terminal app.
home.install.more: Windows and Linux get the x64 builds here. All downloads has the Arm builds and the terminal app, and the installation guide has the first start on each.
home.open.title: Open source
home.open.lede: anistream is developed on GitHub. Anyone can write a plugin or run a store.
apps.title: anistream apps · {{platforms}}
apps.description: The anistream apps for {{platforms}}. You add sources as plugins, and the apps host no content.
apps.head.iconAlt: The anistream app icon: Nagare, the mascot, on the dusk ground
apps.head.title: anistream for {{platforms}}
apps.head.lede: Browsing needs no account, and episodes play inside the app. Your history syncs to your trackers. You add sources as plugins.
apps.toolkits.title: Toolkits
apps.toolkits.text: Each app is built with its platform’s toolkit, and all of them share one engine, written in Rust.
apps.mac.title: Mac
apps.mac.text: A sidebar for Continue, the calendar, seasonal charts, search, your library and downloads, with Settings in the same window. Play turns the window into the player, and Picture in Picture keeps the episode going while you browse. On a Mac, the app and the terminal app share one history and one config.
apps.mac.needs: macOS 26 or later, on Apple silicon
apps.mac.continueAlt: The Mac app on Continue: a banner for the show in progress with a button to resume its episode, and the other shows in progress beside it
apps.mac.titleAlt: The Mac app on a title page: the poster, a button to resume episode 7, the seasons and the episode list
apps.mac.calendarAlt: The Mac app’s calendar, with the week’s episodes laid out by day
apps.iphone.title: iPhone
apps.iphone.text: Tabs for Continue, the calendar, seasonal charts, your library and search. A title page opens from its cover, and the player turns to landscape when an episode starts.
apps.iphone.continueAlt: The iPhone app on Continue, with the show in progress at the top
apps.iphone.titleAlt: The iPhone app on a title page, with a button to resume episode 7
apps.iphone.calendarAlt: The iPhone app’s calendar for the week
apps.ipad.title: iPad
apps.ipad.text: The iPhone app with a sidebar. Title pages put the episode list next to the show’s details, and the calendar shows the whole week.
apps.ipad.continueAlt: The iPad app on Continue, with the sidebar open
apps.ipad.titleAlt: The iPad app on a title page, with the episode list beside the show’s details
apps.ipad.calendarAlt: The iPad app’s calendar for the week
apps.android.title: Android phones
apps.android.text: A navigation bar for Continue, the calendar, seasonal charts, your library and search, with predictive back throughout. Episodes play in landscape.
apps.android.titleAlt: The Android app on a title page
apps.android.calendarAlt: The Android app’s calendar for the week
apps.tablet.title: Android tablets and foldables
apps.tablet.text: On a tablet or an unfolded phone the navigation moves to a rail at the side, and a title page sets the show’s details beside its banner, with the episodes in two columns.
apps.tablet.continueAlt: The Android app on a tablet, on Continue
apps.tablet.titleAlt: The Android app on a tablet, on a title page
apps.tablet.calendarAlt: The Android app’s calendar on a tablet
apps.tv.title: Android TV
apps.tv.text: A separate app made for the remote, with large buttons and a rail for search, Continue, the calendar, seasonal charts and your library. The show you’re watching appears in the TV’s Watch Next row. You sign in to trackers and set up torrents from your phone, with no typing on the TV.
apps.tv.needs: Android TV 11 or later, on ARM
apps.tv.continueAlt: The Android TV app on Continue: the show in progress with a large button to resume episode 7, and a row of other shows below
apps.tv.searchAlt: The Android TV app’s search with nothing typed: the on-screen keyboard, filter chips with Adventure picked, and two matching titles
apps.playTv.title: Play on TV
apps.playTv.text: The Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Windows and Linux apps send an episode to the TV app on the same network, once you have paired them with the code or the QR code the TV shows. The TV plays the episode, and your phone or computer works as the remote, with pause, seek, next episode, subtitles, audio and volume. A phone can also type a search on the TV.
apps.playTv.titleAlt: The Android TV app on a title page, with a button to resume episode 7 and the episode list
apps.playTv.remoteAlt: The iPhone app as the TV’s remote: the episode playing, play and seek buttons, subtitles, audio and the TV’s volume
apps.windows.title: Windows
apps.windows.text: A navigation pane for Continue, the calendar, seasonal charts, your library and downloads, and search with filters in the title bar. Episodes play in the window, with the media keys and taskbar buttons, and the mini player stays on top. New episodes and finished downloads show as Windows notifications.
apps.windows.needs: Windows 10 version 2004 or later, on x64 or Arm64
apps.windows.titleAlt: The Windows app on a title page: the poster, a button to resume episode 7 and the episode list
apps.windows.searchAlt: The Windows app’s Browse page: Adventure picked from the genre filter, sorted by popularity, and two matching titles
apps.windows.storesAlt: The Windows app’s plugin stores: the stores you joined, and one store’s plugins with Install and Update buttons
apps.linux.title: Linux
apps.linux.text: An app that fits in on a GNOME desktop, with a sidebar that folds away in a narrow window and a week view for the calendar. New episodes show as desktop notifications, and the media keys work.
apps.linux.needs: An AppImage for x86-64 or ARM64. It needs glibc 2.41 or newer: Ubuntu 25.04 or later, including 26.04 LTS, Fedora 42 or later, or Debian 13. Ubuntu 24.04 is too old for it.
apps.linux.continueAlt: The Linux app on Continue: the shows in progress, and the one picked with a button to resume its episode
apps.linux.titleAlt: The Linux app on a title page, with the season picker, the episode list and a related title
apps.linux.calendarAlt: The Linux app’s calendar, with the week laid out by day
apps.player.title: The player
apps.player.text: Every app has mpv built in, and its controls fade while you watch. It plays MKV files with their styled subtitles and upscales with ArtCNN or Anime4K, as the terminal app does. A button skips the opening, and Up Next comes up at the ending.
apps.player.macAlt: The Mac app’s player, with its controls over the picture
apps.player.iphoneAlt: The iPhone app’s player in landscape
apps.player.androidAlt: The Android app’s player in landscape
apps.player.credit: The player shows こうしす！ #3.1 by OPAP-JP contributors, licensed CC BY 4.0. Every other title and picture on this page is made up.
apps.across.title: Other features
apps.across.widgets.name: Widgets
apps.across.widgets.text: Continue watching and Airing today on the home screen, on Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android.
apps.across.alerts.name: New-episode notifications
apps.across.alerts.text: An alert when a new episode of a show you watch comes out, on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Android, Windows and Linux. They stay off until you turn them on, and each show has its own switch.
apps.across.live.name: Live Activities
apps.across.live.text: On iPhone, the Lock Screen and the Dynamic Island show what’s playing, your downloads and a show about to air.
apps.across.pip.name: Picture in Picture
apps.across.pip.text: The episode keeps playing in a small window while you browse or use another app, on Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android. On Windows and Linux the player shrinks to a mini player.
apps.across.downloads.name: Downloads
apps.across.downloads.text: Episodes download to the device and play offline, with the same history and resume as a stream. Every app but the TV app can keep the next episodes of the shows you watch downloaded.
apps.across.stores.name: Trackers and plugin stores
apps.across.stores.text: Sign in to your trackers and join plugin stores in the app.
apps.across.handoff.name: Handoff, Spotlight and Shortcuts
apps.across.handoff.text: On Apple devices, pick up a title on another of your devices, find your shows in Spotlight, and ask Siri to continue watching.
apps.download.title: Download
apps.download.lede: The apps aren’t in the App Store or on Google Play, so the first install takes one extra step, covered in the installation guide. After that they update themselves, iPhone and iPad through SideStore or AltStore.
apps.download.legal: Plugins and sources are yours to add, and what you point them at is your decision and your risk, under the laws that apply to you.
apps.download.privacy: What the apps send, and what they keep on your device, is on the privacy page.
features.title: anistream features
features.description: anistream’s features, and which app has each one.
features.apps.title: Apps
features.apps.text: Apps for {{platforms}}, and one for the terminal.
features.apps.macVideoAlt: The Mac app on Continue: another show picked from the queue, its banner growing into the title page, then its second season
features.apps.macAlt: The Mac app on Continue, with a button to resume the show in progress
features.apps.iphoneVideoAlt: The iPhone app on Continue: the show’s banner zooms into its title page, on to its second season, then back home
features.apps.iphoneAlt: The iPhone app on a title page, with a button to resume episode 7
features.apps.androidVideoAlt: The Android app opening a show from Continue, switching to Season 2 and back, scrolling its episodes, then swiping back to Continue
features.apps.windowsAlt: The Windows app on a title page
features.apps.tvAlt: The Android TV app on Continue, with a large button to resume episode 7
features.find.title: Search and the calendar
features.find.text1: Browse by genre, year and season without an account, or follow the seasonal charts and the week’s calendar.
features.find.text2: A ~ marks an estimated air time, and a Dub tag marks an episode already dubbed. Title pages say how far the dub goes, such as “Dub to episode 6”.
features.find.macVideoAlt: The Mac app’s search: Trending now opened in full, the filters panel sliding in, Fantasy taking half the titles away, then a show’s page and its first season
features.find.macAlt: The Mac app’s search, with a query, its two results and the filters panel open: genres, tags, years and length
features.find.phoneVideoAlt: The iPhone app’s calendar: a day picked in the week, a show’s cover zooming into its title page and back, then today again
features.find.phoneAlt: The iPhone app’s calendar: the week’s days, then each day’s episodes with their times
features.player.title: The player
features.player.text: Episodes play in mpv, upscaled by ArtCNN or Anime4K, with the opening and ending marked on the seek bar. Drag the line to compare a 480p stream.
features.player.credit: From こうしす！ #3.2 by OPAP-JP contributors, CC BY 4.0.
features.tv.title: Play on TV
features.tv.text: Send an episode to the Android TV app, then pause, seek and switch subtitles from your phone. The Mac, Windows and Linux apps do the same.
features.tv.phoneVideoAlt: The iPhone app sending an episode to a TV, then pausing it from the remote
features.tv.phoneAlt: The iPhone app as the TV’s remote: the episode playing, play and seek buttons, subtitles, audio and the TV’s volume
features.tv.screenVideoAlt: The Android TV app moving with the remote into a show’s page, switching seasons, then resuming episode 7
features.tv.screenAlt: The Android TV app on a title page, with a button to resume episode 7 and the episode list
features.sync.title: History and sync
features.sync.text: History stays on your device and needs no account. Changes reach your trackers in order, even after a week offline.
features.plugins.title: Plugins and stores
features.plugins.text: Sources are plugins, and each one can reach only the sites it lists. A friend can run a store and invite you.
features.credit: The player in the videos shows こうしす！ #3.1 by OPAP-JP contributors, licensed CC BY 4.0. Every other title and picture in them is made up.
features.diagram.store.alt: A plugin store, invite only, sends its plugin list signed by the store to your devices: a Mac, an iPhone and a Windows PC, each with a token of its own.
features.diagram.sync.alt: Watch history on your device sends each change to a queue, which waits while you are offline and sends the changes in order to AniList, MyAnimeList, Kitsu, Simkl and Trakt. A tracker can move your progress forward, never back.
features.diagram.sync.rule: A tracker can move your progress forward, never back
features.terminalStill.alt: The terminal app on its home screen: the sections down the side, and the show in progress with its cover and how far you are
features.also.title: More features
features.also.watching.skip.name: Skip and Up Next
features.also.watching.skip.text: Skip the opening, and start the next episode from the credits.
features.also.watching.resume.name: Resume
features.also.watching.source.name: Pick a source
features.also.watching.source.text: The automatic pick says why in one line, and you can choose another release.
features.also.watching.dub.name: Sub or dub per show
features.also.watching.dub.text: Set it once and each show remembers.
features.also.watching.tracks.name: Subtitle and audio tracks
features.also.watching.tracks.text: Every app switches the file’s tracks. Mac, Windows and Linux also load a subtitle or audio file.
features.also.watching.pip.name: Picture in Picture
features.also.watching.pip.text: Keep watching while you browse, or in a mini player on Windows and Linux.
features.also.watching.parties.name: Watch parties
features.also.watching.parties.text: Watch with friends in sync, on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, Linux and in the terminal.
features.also.downloads.next.name: Next episodes
features.also.downloads.next.text: The next episodes of your shows download ahead of time.
features.also.downloads.now.name: Start now
features.also.downloads.now.text: Move a queued download to the front.
features.also.downloads.offline.name: Same history offline
features.also.downloads.offline.text: A downloaded episode resumes and syncs like a stream.
features.also.alerts.alerts.name: New-episode alerts
features.also.alerts.alerts.text: Off until you turn them on, per show.
features.also.alerts.widgets.name: Widgets
features.also.alerts.widgets.text: Continue and Airing today on your home screen.
features.also.alerts.handoff.name: Handoff, Spotlight, Shortcuts
features.also.alerts.handoff.text: Pick up a show on another Apple device.
features.also.alerts.live.name: Live Activities
features.also.alerts.live.text: On iPhone, the Lock Screen shows what’s playing, your downloads and a show about to air.
features.also.other.updates.name: Updates
features.also.other.updates.text: The Mac, Android, Android TV, Windows, Linux and terminal apps update themselves.
features.also.other.torrents.name: Torrents on the TV
features.also.other.torrents.text: Scan the TV’s code, then type the index and proxy on your phone.
features.also.other.titles.name: English or romaji
features.also.other.titles.text: Pick how show titles are written.
features.also.other.cli.name: Command line
features.matrix.title: By app
features.matrix.lede: All eight apps have search with filters, the calendar, seasonal charts, subtitle and audio tracks, skip, resume and Up Next. They all sync with AniList, Simkl and Trakt, join plugin stores and run torrents behind the VPN guard. The table shows where they differ.
features.matrix.caption: Which app does each feature
features.matrix.note: Play on TV from the terminal app is in development, and so are home screen widgets on Windows.
